title: Units and Limits That Cannot Be Mixed Up: Speed, Rate, Acceleration and Lateral Acceleration, Shaped Before They Reach a Motor

questions.question: Why make a speed from a named constructor and not a number?
options: The unit is said once, where the number is written
A named constructor is checked at run time
A double cannot hold a speed exactly
It lets the compiler convert units for you
questions.explanation: from_kmh(5.0) and from_mps(5.0) are different words for different speeds. After construction everything is in one unit, at no cost when running.

questions.question: A stop from 1 m/s at 1.5 m/s2 took:
questions.explanation: The time is the speed over the braking, 1 over 1.5. The distance is the speed squared over twice the braking, 1 over 3.

questions.question: 1 m/s with a turn rate of 2 rad/s at a lateral limit of 1.5 m/s2 became:
questions.explanation: Speed times turn rate is the sideways acceleration. To keep it at 1.5 m/s2 with a turn rate of 2 rad/s the speed is cut to 0.75 m/s.

questions.question: A limit of 5 read as m/s when it was km/h made the stopping distance:
options: The same: the brakes are the same
questions.explanation: The speeds differ by 3.6 and the stopping distance goes with the square: 8.331 m against 0.642 m.

questions.question: Why is braking allowed to be stronger than accelerating?
options: It is a rule of the standard
Motors brake harder than they accelerate, and stopping is the safe direction
To make the ramp up smoother
questions.explanation: A stop from 1 m/s took a third of the time and distance of the ramp up to it. Limits should describe the vehicle, and stopping sooner is the safe direction.

questions.question: What does the lateral limit protect against?
options: The wheels slipping on a straight
Tipping or sliding in a turn
questions.explanation: The sideways acceleration in a turn is the speed times the turn rate. Capping it is what keeps a fast, tight turn from tipping or sliding the vehicle.
